name: Emil Kozicki
headline: Software Engineer
summary: Backend-focused software engineer with production experience building and supporting AWS-based integrations and data pipelines in Python. Strongest at diagnosing production failures across systems (AWS, Salesforce, third-party vendor APIs) and shipping features end to end, from data model to UI. M.S. in Computer Science from UNC Charlotte. Left Bridge Investment Group in September 2026 and is currently open to new software engineering roles.

highlights: Supported a fleet of AWS Lambda integrations syncing data between Salesforce and third-party property-management vendors: triaged production failures via Jira and CloudWatch, reconciled drift between live Lambda code and source control, added retry logic for dropped Salesforce connections during large paginated queries, and extended vendor CSV parsing to support new fields without breaking existing exports.

Designed and shipped a Deferred Work Items feature end to end, including the Salesforce data model (Apex changes, a new lifecycle-event object to track item history) and client-side schema migrations and UI in HomeWyze, an existing offline-first SvelteKit PWA.

Resolved a production incident caused by the Deferred Work Items schema change, where devices running stale cached app code submitted payloads that no longer matched the updated backend schema: patched the Lambda to accept both formats, recovered failed submissions by re-running Step Functions executions, and built a background update-detection service that keeps clients on current code without interrupting users.

Monitored and maintained AWS Batch job scheduling across integration pipelines. Diagnosed a queue-wide outage where a job definition's memory requirement exceeded every attached compute environment's capacity, silently blocking ~290 queued jobs; restored the last known-good configuration and added an EventBridge/SNS alert on Batch's queue-blocked events to catch this failure mode automatically.

Designed and shipped a bulk photo-export feature for HomeWorx, a Salesforce-based property inspection platform, spanning a Lightning Web Component, an Apex integration layer with sandbox/production routing and error handling, and a Python Lambda that downloads S3-stored photos concurrently (ThreadPoolExecutor), archives them, and returns a presigned URL for direct download.

projects.name: AI Portfolio Site
projects.tech: React, Vite, Django REST Framework, Google Gemini API
projects.description: This site — a React front end backed by a Django REST API, with an AI assistant that answers visitor questions about my background.
highlights: Built a Django REST endpoint that proxies chat requests to the Gemini API, keeping the API key server-side so it never reaches the browser.

Hardened the assistant against prompt injection and jailbreak attempts by isolating untrusted visitor input in delimited tags, declaring no tools, and enforcing explicit topic and confidentiality boundaries in the system prompt.
Layered abuse protection over the public endpoints: IP-based burst and daily throttles, request length caps, server-side conversation history truncation, and output token limits.
Implemented a contact pipeline that persists submissions to the database before sending SMTP notifications, so messages survive email delivery failures.
Built the front end around CSS custom properties for instant dark/light theming, with canvas-based particle animation and scroll-triggered reveals.

projects.name: CLT Events
projects.description: Full-stack web application for event creation, browsing, RSVP management, and user profile handling.
highlights: Implemented secure user authentication with hashed password verification, session tracking via express-session, and persistent login state stored in connect-mongo.
Built CRUD features for events including image upload handling, date/time validation, category filtering, and RSVP restrictions.
Designed a personalized profile dashboard displaying hosted events and RSVP history by aggregating and populating related MongoDB collections.
Used EJS templating for dynamic server-side rendering with real-time feedback via connect-flash messages.
Applied error handling and access control preventing unauthorized event edits, invalid RSVPs, and duplicate account registration.
